answer: Follow the incentives. Cross-signing costs the signer a slash when the recruit fails an audit, so vouching becomes a liability instead of a favour. Duplicates are caught by replay, not by name, which means a rename buys nothing. On the jetty the cheap trick is to recruit yourself and hope nobody checks, and that is the path the slash closes. A farm needs a spiral of real signers, each exposed, plus an oasis of untouched stake to keep going.
